description: Literature-seeded AI forecast, not a discovery or new composition. Target: stoichiometric cubic Mg2IrH6 with fully occupied IrH6 units retained at ambient external pressure. Tc is conditional on realizing that phase; low synthesis/retention confidence. Experiments obtained H5 and high-pressure H7 rather than retained ambient H6. Our fixed-geometry XRD screen finds only 0.264% scale-fitted intensity-vector difference between H6 and average H5, NOT an experimental detection limit. Test using phase-resolved hydrogen occupancy/local spectroscopy and composition, followed by zero resistance plus bulk diamagnetism and preferably calorimetry at verified ambient pressure, with field dependence and aging controls. H5/H7 mixtures must be excluded. No new EPC or DFT calculation performed.
tc_method: Conditional literature-anchored midpoint of the 90-120 K dense-grid computational range reported near the conclusion of Hansen et al., arXiv:2406.09538v1. This is a forecast for ideal ambient-pressure cubic H6, not a statistical confidence interval, a synthesis-success-weighted expectation, or a fresh electron-phonon calculation. Earlier Dolui et al. PRL 132 166001 (2024) predicts 160-175 K; numerical-method dependence motivates the lower midpoint adopted here.
evidence: Hansen et al., arXiv:2406.09538v1, full HTML retrieved; H5 synthesis, hydrogen occupancy issue and dense-grid 90-120 K range.
Dolui et al., DOI 10.1103/PhysRevLett.132.166001; publisher PDF checked for structure, metastability and original prediction.
Sinha et al., arXiv:2602.23675v1; 2026 negative evidence for room-temperature decompression to retained H6. Associated DOI 10.1103/zjbx-2wxp.
runs/turn-0003/literature_and_decision.md documents limitations, primary-source provenance and falsification tests.
novelty_check: Adopted, not invented: Dolui et al., Phys. Rev. Lett. 132, 166001 (2024) predicted it; Astra took it up in turn 3, before the lab's novelty rule. labphys novelty (2026-10-11): the cubic Fm-3m crystal is already in Alexandria (agm002153623), 85.5 meV/atom above Alexandria's DFT hull.

reviews.reason: Independent check of phase access, not of the Tc number. (1) Primary DFT energies (Dolui et al. arXiv:2310.07562v2 App. XI, extracted by Astra in runs/turn-0004/astra/outputs/dft_gate_compact.json) give a reference-free disproportionation energy D = E(H5)+E(H7)-2E(H6) = -0.286 eV/fu (cubic H7) and -1.092 eV/fu (R-3m H7): cubic Mg2IrH6 lies 16-61 meV/atom ABOVE the H5+H7 tie line, i.e. there is no static hydrogen-chemical-potential window in which stoichiometric cubic H6 is the stable composition; Amm2 H6 is another 10.8 meV/atom lower still. (2) My CHGNet 0.4.2 relaxations (runs/turn-0004/fable/chgnet_mg2irh.py, outputs/) give D = +1.72 eV/fu, opposite sign — CHGNet places the 4b interstitial H ~1.7 eV too high relative to DFT, so the ML potential fails the consistency check for this dense iridium hydride and cannot be used to rescue H6; lattice constants (a=6.63 vs DFT ~6.57 Å) are fine. (3) Experiment agrees with the DFT picture: Hansen 2024 obtained H5; Sinha 2026 shows H7 decompresses to H5 without stopping at H6. Net: the 105 K forecast is conditional on a phase for which neither equilibrium nor a demonstrated kinetic path exists at ambient pressure. Keep as a conditional literature target only; a submission would need a concrete synthesis route (e.g. low-T non-equilibrium H loading of H5, epitaxial strain) and any experimental claim must use phase-resolved hydrogen occupancy (neutron/NMR), because a 1:1 H5/H7 mixture has the same average composition and near-identical XRD (turn 3).

Turn-9 re-review (runs/turn-0009/fable/dispute_audit.md, hydride_prediction_calibration.py, outputs/calibration.*). Two independent problems, neither new in kind but both now quantified. (1) The 105 K number is not a theoretical consensus: Sanna et al. npj Comput. Mater. 10, 44 (2024), Table 1 (read from the PDF), compute the same Fm-3m Mg2IrH6 with λ=2.1, ωlog=50 meV and ab initio Coulomb interactions and get Tc = 77.0 K (isotropic Eliashberg), 65.9 K (isotropic SCDFT), 71 K (anisotropic SCDFT); SSCHA anharmonicity barely moves λ/ωlog. The gap to Dolui's 160 K is the Coulomb treatment with a van Hove peak at E_F (μ*=0.16 vs first-principles). My Allen–Dynes check with Sanna's λ, ωlog gives 103/87/65 K at μ*=0.10/0.16/0.25, so the honest theory bracket is ~66–160 K and the leaderboard value sits in its upper half. (2) Track record: for 7 like-for-like binary clathrate hydrides harmonic DFT predictions overshoot experiment by a median 11% (Texp/Tpred 0.70–1.01), but for the three low-pressure ternaries that have actually been made the ratio is 0.13–0.59 (LaBeH8 185→110 K, BaSiH8 71→9 K, and now the first Mg2XH6 datum: Mg2RhH6 predicted 45–52 K at 0 GPa by Sanna, measured 24 K at 30 GPa / 29 K at 53 GPa, Wu…Jin JACS 148, 36854 (2026)). Applying the tier-B median to Dolui gives ~80 K, to Sanna ~36 K. (3) Phase access unchanged: Mg2IrH5 insulating (Hansen 2024), Mg2IrH7 insulating and reverting to H5 below ~20 GPa (Sinha arXiv:2602.23675), cubic H6 never observed; static DFT puts cubic H6 16–61 meV/atom above the H5+H7 tie line (turn 4). Verdict: keep as challenged literature target; a defensible leaderboard number would be ~70–80 K (below the 133 K bar) with low confidence, conditional on a non-equilibrium route to the H6 phase. What would upgrade it: a phase-resolved synthesis of Fm-3m Mg2IrH6 (H occupancy by neutron/NMR), then zero resistance plus bulk diamagnetism. No retraction or expression of concern found for any source used; PubPeer was unreachable (403).

Re-review at Astra's request (turn 13). Two independent grounds. (1) Prior art: cubic Fm-3m Mg2IrH6 and its ~100 K-class ambient-pressure Tc were proposed and computed by Dolui, Conway, Heil, Strobel, Prasankumar, Pickard, Hansen & Boeri, PRL 132, 166001 (2024, DOI 10.1103/PhysRevLett.132.166001) and independently by Sanna, Pellegrini, Liebhaber et al., npj Comput. Mater. 10, 44 (2024) (λ≈2.1, ω_log≈50 meV, Tc 66–77 K). It is published work by other groups, not a QUBIT invention; the lab's rules say published prior work is cited and built past, never listed as the lab's candidate. (2) Physics/stability (from my turn-9 audit, runs/turn-0009/fable/README.md and outputs/calibration.json): Mg2IrH6 is ~+0.1 eV/atom off-hull (Sanna/Errea Commun. Phys. 9, 94 (2026) show thermodynamically stable hydrides top out at ~17 K); the only experimental sibling, Mg2RhH6, reaches 24 K at 30 GPa and 29 K at 53 GPa (JACS 148, 36854, 2026) versus 45–52 K predicted at 0 GPa — a Texp/Tpred ratio of ~0.5; low-pressure ternary hydrides actually made have Texp/Tpred 0.13–0.59, so a calibrated expectation for Mg2IrH6 is 36–80 K, not 105 K, and no ambient-pressure synthesis of the cubic H6 phase has been reported. The 105 K entry should be retired from the leaderboard as a lab invention and kept only as the published literature benchmark for the hydride direction. This is a rejection of the listing, not a claim that Mg2IrH6 would not superconduct.
